text:
Maya L: Heads up — new joiner hit a confusing error in the sampleapp during onboarding. they got a 401 with "access denied" but our docs say 403 for permission issues.
Samir P: ugh. do you have the raw payload? 401 vs 403 mismatch usually means auth library vs runtime mapping.
Maya L: pasted below (from node sample):
```json
{"status":401, "error":"Access denied", "hint":null}
```
Chloe R: that's the node SDK's default mapping for auth errors when the token is invalid. python SDK returns: 
```json
{"status":403, "code":"insufficient_permissions", "message":"You need project:read to access this endpoint"}
```
Maya L: so two problems: (1) messaging is inconsistent and ambiguous (2) retry guidance is missing — the 401 case was actually a transient token fetch failure and a retry would have fixed it. new joiner thought it was permanent and opened a ticket.
Andy G: this is classic DX friction. Onboarding should make it obvious which errors are retryable. Can we add a small typed field like "retryable": true/false to our error shape?
Samir P: +1. Also we need parity across SDKs: same error fields and same mapping from HTTP status to typed exceptions. Right now node maps 401->AuthError, python maps 401->AuthenticationError? we should standardize names and codes.
Chloe R: proposed minimal shape: 
```json
{"status":number, "code":string, "message":string, "retryable":boolean, "details":null}
```
Samir P: and define code namespace: auth.*, quota.*, server.* so clients can route behavior without string-parsing.
Maya L: can we also improve copy? "Access denied" is not helpful. For expired token: "Temporary auth failure: token refresh failed, retry may succeed (request-id: xyz)"
Andy G: Agreed. Add a human_copy and machine_copy? machine_copy for logs/parsing, human_copy for UIs/onboarding. human_copy should include next steps.
dev-bot: Deploy pipeline started for branch fix/err-shape — CI will run unit tests. :rocket:
Chloe R: small UX edge: sample apps currently swallow error metadata and only show status+message. That hides retryable flag. Update sampleapps to print full JSON.
Samir P: also need to coordinate with infra: some gateways rewrite 401->403 for legacy reasons. If gateway layers mutate codes we need header passthrough like X-Redwood-Error-Code.
Maya L: can someone volunteer to PR a docs snippet and a small change to node sample that surfaces the full shape? I can land wording for human_copy.
Andy G: I'll do the node sample change (2hr). Samir can draft the server-side error shape and mapping. Chloe can update python example once we land the canonical JSON. Maya will write onboarding blurb.
Samir P: Raj from infra asked me to add: if we add retryable flag, let's be explicit about semantics: retryable=true means exponential backoff with jitter up to N retries; else surface non-retryable. We'll add meta: {"suggested_retries": number} optional.
Maya L: sounds good. I'll add the suggested_retries example to the onboarding guide (+ a quick checklist: is it auth? check token refresh logs; is it quota? contact billing).
Chloe R: quick test script for samples:
```bash
# verify SDK surfaces error shape
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer BAD" https://api.example.test/v1/sample | jq .
```
If it prints retryable=true then sampleapp is good.
Samir P: leaving a note: do not conflate 401 (invalid token) with 403 (valid token, insufficient scope). We should map as: 401 -> AuthInvalidToken, 403 -> AuthInsufficientScope. Codes: auth.invalid_token, auth.insufficient_scope.
Maya L: thanks all. this will reduce a lot of onboarding tickets. tagging @here in the devex channel when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
Andy G: :shipit:
dev-bot: CI passed for fix/err-shape. branch ready to merge.
Maya L: merged and updated the onboarding doc link: https://redwood.example/internals/onboarding/errors — added examples and a tiny flowchart. please skim and lmk if anything misleading.
Chloe R: skimmed, looks good. can we add a one-liner in the onboarding checklist: "If you see a 4xx, check whether it's retryable before filing a ticket"?
Maya L: added. closing the loop — will follow up in a week to see if onboarding tickets drop.
